claims.text: ALD of a sub-monolayer of Pt on oxygen-vacancy-rich Ce0.5Zr0.5O2 creates atomically dispersed Pt species.
The proposed ALD treatment creates sub-nanometric Pt clusters.
Atomically dispersed Pt and sub-nanometric Pt clusters enhance catalytic activity.
The proposed catalyst architecture improves durability.
The proposed catalyst architecture reduces overall Pt consumption.
Conventional Pt nanoparticle catalysts on standard Ce0.5Zr0.5O2 or gamma-Al2O3 use higher Pt loadings.
Conventional Pt nanoparticle catalysts suffer sintering during high-temperature redox cycling.
Oxygen vacancies in Ce0.5Zr0.5O2 stabilize isolated Pt atoms and sub-nanometric clusters through strong metal-support interactions.
ALD promotes the formation of isolated Pt atoms and very small Pt clusters on the support.
Oxygen vacancies anchor the isolated Pt atoms and small Pt clusters.
The vacancy-anchored Pt sites facilitate conversion of CO, hydrocarbons, and NOx.
Stabilization of Pt at oxygen vacancies prevents Pt sintering during harsh redox cycling.
Preventing Pt sintering maintains catalytic activity and durability at lower Pt loading.
Relative to conventional impregnated catalysts, the ALD-prepared catalyst will maintain or improve conversion efficiencies for CO, hydrocarbons, and NOx.
The ALD-prepared catalyst can reduce Pt loading by approximately 50% while maintaining performance.
The ALD-prepared catalyst will exhibit enhanced thermal stability and minimal Pt sintering after prolonged high-temperature cycling.
The predicted benefits will hold at 400–800°C under alternating oxidizing and reducing environments.
Performance is sensitive to ALD deposition uniformity and the precision of oxygen-vacancy engineering.
